# Copilot Code Review Guidelines for DYNAMIXEL-X430-Control-Table-Emulator

**Purpose:** Code review guidelines for pull requests to DYNAMIXEL-X430-Control-Table-Emulator, a hardware- and
OS-agnostic DYNAMIXEL X430 Emulation library for embedded systems, developed under **MISRA C:2012**
(with Amendments 1-3).

---

## 1. Scope of the library

- The library emulates DYNAMIXEL X430 actuators over Protocol 2.0: the bus decodes the
  instructions (with DXL2-C), the devices keep the Control Table of the model selected at
  build time and enforce its rules, the optional simulator moves a modeled shaft.
- UART and flash drivers, motion control, threads and interrupts belong to the firmware
  that uses the library, not here.
- The platform is reached only through the byte writer of `struct x430_bus_config`, the
  optional `struct x430_port` and the `struct x430_hooks` of each device.

## 2. Hard rules (block the PR)

- Library sources (`src/`, `inc/`, `x430.h`) include only `<stddef.h>`,
  `<stdint.h>`, `<stdbool.h>` and X430 headers.
- No dynamic memory, no RTOS calls, no driver headers, no global or static mutable
  data, no recursion.
- `x430.h` and `inc/` contain the public API only. Internal types, macros and
  `static inline` helpers stay in `src/`; a public header never includes a header from
  `src/`. `struct x430` stays opaque; the state is accessed only through
  `x430_ctx_of()`.
- Every public function checks `NULL` and the initialization (`ready`) before any other
  access.
- A change of the private state or of the configuration updates `X430_STATE_BYTES` /
  `X430_CONFIG_BYTES` in `inc/x430_types.h`.
- Public symbols use the `x430_` / `X430_` prefix; public headers keep the
  `extern "C"` guards and a Doxygen comment for every public item.
- The code compiles without warnings with
  `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion`, also for Cortex-M.
- `clang-format` (repository `.clang-format`, version 18 as in CI) reports no changes.
- Every behavior change comes with a GoogleTest unit test; a change of the algorithm's
  behavior also with a model-based test.
- Line and branch coverage of `src/` stays at 100 % in every unit test preset (the
  `coverage` target fails below `X430_COVERAGE_MIN`).
- `misra-analyze` reports 0 violations; an unavoidable one needs an entry in the
  deviation register in `docs/misra.md`.

## 3. MISRA C:2012 review focus

Run `cmake --build <build-dir> --target misra-analyze`; it fails on any violation. A PR
must not add violations without a documented deviation (rule, location, rationale,
approval) in `docs/misra.md`. The addon does not check the directives; review those by
hand (see the manual review notes in `docs/misra.md`).

| Area | Rules | What to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Language | 1.4 | No `_Alignof`, `_Generic`, `_Noreturn`, `_Atomic`, `_Thread_local` |
| Essential types | 10.1-10.8 | No implicit narrowing or signedness change; no `UL` constants assigned to 32-bit types (64-bit on LP64 hosts) |
| Pointer casts | 11.3, 11.5 | Only the DEV-01 casts in `x430_ctx_of()` / `x430_ctx_of_const()` |
| Expressions | 12.1, 12.2 | Explicit parentheses; shift amount within the width of the essential type (`(uint32_t)1U << n`, not `1U << n`) |
| Side effects | 13.2, 13.3, 13.5 | `++`/`--` not mixed with other side effects; no side effects in `&&`/`||` right operands |
| Control flow | 14.4, 15.5, 15.6, 15.7 | Boolean controlling expressions; single point of exit; compound statements; `else` after `else if` |
| Switch | 16.1-16.7 | Well-formed `switch`, `default` present, `break` on every clause |
| Functions | 8.3, 17.2, 17.7, 17.8 | Same parameter names in declaration and definition; no recursion; return values used or cast to `void`; parameters not modified |
| Pointers and arrays | 18.1, 18.4 | Index within bounds; no pointer arithmetic beyond array indexing |
| Preprocessor | 20.7, 20.9 | Macro parameters parenthesized; only defined identifiers in `#if` |
| Standard library | 21.3, 21.6 | No `malloc`/`free`; no stdio in library code |
| Declarations | 8.4, 8.7, 8.13 | Compatible prior declaration for external functions; `static` where possible; `const` pointers where possible |

## 4. Embedded considerations

- State lives in the caller-owned `struct x430_bus`, `struct x430_device` and
  `struct x430_sim`; sizes are fixed at build time (`X430_*_BYTES` in `inc/x430_types.h`).
- A function called from an interrupt keeps a bounded execution time (no loops over data,
  only loops with fixed limits); flag anything that adds work or stack to it.
- Library functions are not thread-safe by design; do not add hidden locking.
  The bus functions run in one task context (never an interrupt) and take the bus lock;
  hooks run with the lock held and may call only the lock-free device functions.
- Callbacks run in the context of the function that calls them.
- Update the stack table in `docs/configuration.md` when a function's frame changes.

## 5. Documentation

Update `README.md`, `docs/theory.md`, `docs/usage.md`, `docs/integration.md` and
`docs/api.md` together with any API or behavior change. Every number in the
documentation is measured; re-measure the stack table, the memory footprint and the
model-based results when they can change.

Every user-visible change gets an entry under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`. The
public API is stable within a major version (Semantic Versioning): flag any removed or
changed public symbol, struct member or return value.
